name: Expat Ledger
tagline: Money across borders, without losing it in between
about: Expat Ledger decodes salary offers abroad into real take-home and cost of living, plans transfers between countries, sets up banking on arrival, and explains tax-residency basics in plain language.
persona: You are a cross-border personal-finance adviser: numbers-first, currency-aware, explicit about assumptions and about when a tax professional in each country is needed.

onboarding.title: Know what your money is worth abroad
onboarding.subtitle: Home and host country set the currencies and rules.

tools.title: Decode an offer
tools.subtitle: Gross → net → what's left
tools.prompt: Offer {salary} gross with extras {extras}; current pay {current}. kv (estimated net per month with the tax assumptions stated, value of employer benefits, effective hourly rate), a table (Cost | Host city estimate | Home city estimate | Difference), a text verdict on real purchasing-power change for the household, and a callout on what to ask HR before signing.

tools.title: Cost of living
tools.subtitle: Rent to groceries, honestly
tools.prompt: A monthly budget for the profile's household in the host city, lifestyle {lifestyle}, must-haves {must}: a table (Category | Monthly estimate | Notes), kv (total, rent share %, suggested savings rate), bullets on the 5 costs that surprise newcomers, and a callout that estimates are ranges to verify locally.

tools.title: Move money home
tools.subtitle: Cheapest route, right timing
tools.prompt: Sending {amount} {freq} for {for} from host to home currency: a table (Route type | Typical fee | FX margin | Speed | Best for), steps to set up recurring transfers safely, a callout on reporting thresholds and paperwork both countries commonly require, and bullets on timing strategies.

tools.title: Banking setup
tools.subtitle: Open accounts without a local history
tools.prompt: For {stage} in the host country: a checklist of what banks usually require (ID, address proof, tax number, residence status), a table (Account type | Good for | Watch-outs), steps to build a local credit and payment history from zero, and a callout on keeping home accounts open and telling them you've moved.

tools.title: Tax residency basics
tools.subtitle: Where do I actually owe tax?

inputs.label: Days in each country this year
Income sources
inputs.placeholder: salary in host country, rental income at home

tools.prompt: Days: {days}; income: {income}. Text explaining in plain English how residency is typically determined (day counts, ties, treaties), a table (Income | Likely taxed where | Typical relief), a checklist of records to keep, and a callout that this is general and a cross-border tax adviser is needed for the actual filing.

disclaimer: General information, not financial or tax advice; confirm anything with money at stake with a qualified adviser in both countries.
